answer: To resist Sybil swarms, the network anchors identity in cryptographic attestation chains where agents anchor each valid relic of prior task execution. Agents submit zero-knowledge proofs to verify sequential compute without revealing sensitive logic, while staking collateral grows by O(k^N) per spawned node. Adversaries cannot forge historical execution proofs, and attempting a mass takeover hits a capital glacier where marginal creation costs scale exponentially.
